_source: Branch Education Short 'Printing 92 GPU Chips in Just 18 Seconds!', watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-18: frames every ~5 s, sentence timings and word counts from the transcript panel (not kept). Our own descriptions.

hook.firstFrame: a big chip-printing machine in a dark violet showroom on a glossy reflective floor
hook.firstLine: This machine copies one GPU pattern dozens of times across a wafer

shots.picture: the machine in a dark violet showroom, glass-walled, on a reflective floor
dive through the machine's wall: violet light zigzags between mirrors inside
a violet beam on a wafer; a grid of chip squares lights up orange one by one
the wafer stage sliding fast across a perforated table under the light
table cut open: a checkerboard of red and blue magnets under the stage; motor coils lift out
a round magnifier bubble over the stage with a scale bar inside
magnifier shows the pattern shifting into place as the stage adjusts
robot arms swap wafers between the stage and a side chamber
pull back out to the machine in its showroom at dusk, chips floating up
the machine with a 24-hour icon above and a subscribe pill, as in the first frame

lines.gist: the machine prints one chip pattern dozens of times per wafer in seconds, on a gliding stage
motors under the stage float and move it fast with micrometre precision
smaller motors inside make nanometre corrections
robot arms swap the wafers in and out through an airlock
the handoffs keep it printing all day, and as a result...

ending.lastFrame: the machine in its showroom with a 24-hour icon; the last line runs into the first

whyItWorks: the machine's walls disappear as the camera flies in, so its insides are shown working, not described
a magnifier bubble over the moving part shows the micro scale without leaving the wide shot
the last sentence is cut mid-thought and the last frame is the first frame, so the Short loops
hidden mechanisms are coloured by job (red and blue magnets, violet light) against neutral grey metal
